papers.title: Lifespan Trajectories of Resting State Bipolar EEG Power
papers.summary: Derived normative lifespan trajectories of resting-state bipolar EEG power from 12,906 observations (ages 12–70) in 5,781 alcohol-use-disorder-free COGA participants across seven frequency bands and 24 channels. Found sharp power decreases from ages 12 to early 20s, followed by beta increases and mixed theta/alpha patterns, with sagittal and lateral trajectories similar within and between sexes but bipolar inter-frequency correlations showing striking sex differences.

papers.title: Secondary exploratory discrete wavelet analysis of the electroretinogram in adults with ADHD.
papers.summary: Applied discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to electroretinogram (ERG) recordings from 25 adults with ADHD and 25 matched controls across seven flash intensities to extract multiscale time-frequency descriptors. Found lower global 40a and 20b DWT values in ADHD (dz = -0.63 and -0.60; FDR q = 0.020), consistent across sexes, eyes, medication strata, and sensitivity analyses, with exploratory classification AUCs of 0.653–0.731.

papers.title: Polysomnographic Sleep in Idiopathic Nightmares: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of polysomnographic differences between individuals with idiopathic nightmares and healthy controls, including 14 case-control studies with 7 studies (112 cases, 112 controls) in the meta-analysis. Found no significant differences in sleep macro-architecture (total sleep time, wake after sleep onset, sleep stage percentages), while limited micro-architecture and autonomic data precluded confident conclusions.

papers.title: A generalized scaling law reveals synchrony-driven reorganization of brain dynamics across human lifespan.
papers.summary: The authors generalized Taylor's law to neural data by replacing the sample mean with the root mean square and applied it to detrended multivariate fMRI time series, showing analytically and in simulations that the scaling exponent is inversely related to synchrony. In three large human cohorts (N=840, ages 18–88), the scaling exponent showed age-related trajectories and synchrony-induced reduction, with altered synchrony-scaling coupling in ADHD.

papers.title: Distinct EEG microstate signatures across different pain types
papers.summary: Applied a harmonized EEG microstate analysis pipeline across three pain conditions—capsaicin-induced pain, non-chronic back pain, and chronic back pain—compared with matched controls or pain-free baseline. Found pain-type-specific microstate signatures: capsaicin pain increased microstate C expression and transitions toward C, non-chronic back pain showed lower microstate C occurrence, and chronic back pain showed lower microstate D global explained variance, arguing against a unitary microstate signature of pain.

papers.title: A Semi-Dry, Visually Comfortable c-VEP BCI with Short Calibration, Conservative Idle-State Behavior, and a VR Proof of Concept
papers.summary: Developed and evaluated a semi-dry, low-salience c-VEP brain-computer interface with slow flashing codes, asynchronous evidence accumulation, and conservative idle-state behavior in 30 participants. Achieved 99.8% accuracy with 33 s calibration and 4.3 s mean decoding in an 11-class keypad task, no spurious commands during a 2-min idle period, and 100% accuracy with 5.6 s decoding in a VR proof-of-concept, with high visual comfort but higher fatigue in VR.

papers.title: Dynamic Phase Synchrony in Cortical Networks Underlying Conscious Awareness of Flicker.
papers.summary: Using EEG near the critical flicker-fusion frequency, the study found that conscious flicker perception is characterized by early higher beta-band synchrony followed by gamma-band synchrony between fronto-parietal and parieto-occipital regions around 300 ms, alongside global gamma power expansion; fused perception showed stronger alpha-band synchrony reduction. These frequency-specific coordination patterns suggest a role for large-scale network dynamics in visual awareness.

papers.title: Spatial Sampling and Temporal Dynamics Shape Motor Decoding from Broadband Intracortical Signals
papers.summary: Comparing broadband intracortical signals in monkeys, the study found that spiking-band power and high-frequency LFP decoding scaled with single-unit count, whereas local motor potential decoding depended more on electrode geometry and performed better with planar Utah arrays; LMP decoding was dominated by low-frequency delta-band components (0.1–8 Hz). Nonlinear temporal decoders further improved LMP decoding, highlighting spatial sampling and temporal structure for motor brain-computer interfaces.

papers.title: EEG emotion recognition via multilevel entropy analysis: The power of entropy of entropy on phase dynamics.
papers.summary: This study introduced Entropy of Entropy (EoE) applied to EEG phase series for emotion recognition, comparing it with phase entropy, Shannon entropy, and amplitude EoE on the GAMEEMO dataset. EoE-phase features significantly outperformed traditional entropy measures, achieving 71.7% accuracy and 0.869 AUC with a Random Forest classifier.

papers.title: EEG Signatures Support a Shrinking Spotlight of Attention After Errors.
papers.summary: In a luminance-varying flanker task with EEG and hierarchical sequential sampling modeling, post-error adjustments involved frontal midline theta linked to increased decision threshold and faster drift rate, while posterior alpha/beta power scaled with drift rate and this relationship was enhanced after errors. The findings support separable roles of midfrontal control and sensory-specific attentional mechanisms in adaptive control.

papers.title: Evoked alpha oscillatory activity is suppressed by prolonged elbow pain and modulated by repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation.
papers.summary: In secondary analyses of two experiments using nerve growth factor-induced prolonged elbow pain, TMS-EEG showed reduced alpha event-related spectral perturbation and intertrial coherence at peak pain compared with baseline, and active 10-Hz rTMS increased alpha ERSP relative to sham without altering ITC. The results suggest evoked alpha activity as a candidate marker of pain state and neuromodulation response.

papers.title: Repetitive negative thinking is associated with conflict-related neural activity that modulates evidence accumulation.
papers.journal: Journal of mood and anxiety disorders
papers.summary: In 37 participants completing a flanker task with EEG and hierarchical drift diffusion modeling, higher repetitive negative thinking was associated with a more negative midfrontal conflict N2 and larger congruent-incongruent drift-rate differences, and the N2 mediated the relationship between RNT and drift-rate modulation. The findings link RNT to heightened conflict-related neural activity that increases context-sensitive evidence accumulation.

papers.title: Effective connectivity in the active encoding of facial emotions: a dynamic causal modeling study.
papers.summary: Using dynamic causal modeling on EEG data from 62 participants performing a delayed match-to-sample task with facial emotions, this study examined effective connectivity among six nodes in bilateral occipital, temporal, and frontal regions during encoding. Results showed early encoding modulated widespread connectivities including reduced bottom-up excitation and strengthened top-down inhibition, while later encoding involved a subset of top-down effects, with modulation strength not reliably linked to behavior.

papers.title: Beyond processed depth targets: frontal EEG patterns, brain vulnerability, and postoperative delirium in older adults.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
papers.summary: This narrative review examined whether frontal EEG signals beyond processed depth indices provide information about postoperative delirium risk in older adults, synthesizing evidence from randomized trials, systematic reviews, and observational studies. It concluded that processed EEG-guided titration alone does not reliably prevent delirium, but patterns such as reduced alpha power, burst suppression, and spectral slowing may reflect anesthetic sensitivity and reduced cerebral reserve, supporting contextual interpretation.

papers.title: Transdiagnostic patterns of electroencephalography (EEG)-derived aperiodic activity across schizophrenia-spectrum, bipolar, and depressive disorders: A systematic review.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized 30 peer-reviewed studies (N=2298) on EEG-derived aperiodic activity in schizophrenia-spectrum, bipolar, and depressive disorders. It found heterogeneous results in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders (steeper slopes, higher offsets, reduced temporal flexibility), flatter slopes and reduced offsets in major depressive and treatment-resistant depression (especially central/posterior), limited bipolar evidence, and treatment sensitivity, suggesting aperiodic parameters may be more useful as context-sensitive within-subject markers than fixed diagnostic signatures.

papers.title: Optimization of visibility-adaptive expressway early warning schemes under sand-dust weather considering driver workload.
papers.summary: A driving-simulator study with 36 drivers optimized visibility-adaptive multimodal early warning schemes (VMS, LED guidance, voice) across four sand-dust visibility levels. The optimal scheme significantly improved speed compliance by 10.6 percentage points (to 89.2%), reduced steering and lateral acceleration deviations, lowered heart rate by 4.28 bpm, and raised the EEG β/θ ratio by 0.14 at 500 m and 300 m visibility.

papers.title: Desflurane Increases Hippocampal RAF-MAPK-MSK1 Protein Levels and Reduces CLOCK Expression: Sorafenib Attenuates Cognitive Impairment in Aged Mice.
papers.summary: In aged mice and HT22 hippocampal neurons, desflurane exposure increased RAF-MAPK-MSK1 protein levels and reduced CLOCK, accompanied by cellular senescence, synaptic imbalance, and cognitive deficits. The RAF inhibitor sorafenib restored CLOCK, attenuated senescence markers, and improved cognitive performance, suggesting RAF inhibition as a potential strategy for desflurane-induced cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Respiration and individual differences shape behavioral and inter-brain synchronization
papers.summary: This hyperscanning EEG study of 88 individuals in musical synchronization tasks found that instructed in-phase and anti-phase breathing increased inter-brain phase-locking and perceived social closeness but reduced behavioral synchrony. Inhalation was linked to stronger inter-brain synchronization but less precise behavioral coordination, and partners with faster spontaneous production rates led with alpha-band phase advances.

papers.title: When the Electromyography (EMG) and the Patient Disagree: Unraveling a Motor Neuron Disease Mimic With Small-Fiber Dysfunction.
papers.summary: A case report describes a 52-year-old man with an eight-year history of muscle twitching, tremor, tightness, and asymmetric cutaneous hypersensitivity initially suggestive of diffuse motor neuron disease on EMG. Repeat evaluation revealed focal ulnar neurogenic abnormalities and left L5-S1 radiculopathy without evidence of neurodegeneration, and sudomotor testing showed reduced electrochemical skin conductance in the hands indicating small-fiber/autonomic dysfunction; symptomatic treatment with gabapentin and vitamin E yielded approximately 80% improvement after six weeks.

papers.title: Positive interactions and active mentalizing facilitate inter-brain synchronization in couples.
papers.summary: Using EEG hyperscanning in 42 romantic couples during naturalistic positive and negative interactions, this study found that beta-band inter-brain synchronization was higher during positive compared to negative interactions. Mentalizing versus counting increased alpha- and beta-band synchronization, supporting inter-brain synchronization as a marker of interaction valence and sociocognitive engagement.

papers.title: Quantitative assessment of cervical spinal cord injury: Methods, clinical utility, and future directions.
papers.journal: The journal of spinal cord medicine
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized 73 publications on quantitative assessment methods for cervical spinal cord injury, covering imaging, neurological scales, electrophysiology, biomechanics, wearable sensors, and AI. It concluded that current methods are insufficient alone and proposed a staged multimodal strategy integrating wearable sensing and AI to improve clinical management and prognosis.

papers.title: A neuroeducational approach to STEM education: Integrating real-time cognitive analysis and cognitive load theory to optimize teaching and learning at universities.
papers.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
papers.summary: A systematic narrative review with cross-case synthesis examined peer-reviewed empirical studies (2018–2025) integrating real-time cognitive analysis tools (e.g., EEG, fNIRS, eye tracking, AI analytics) with Cognitive Load Theory in university STEM education. Synthesis indicated that real-time cognitive feedback positively influenced teaching effectiveness (d = 0.68–0.72, P < 0.01), multimodal analytics improved cognitive load estimation, and cognitively based personalization reduced cognitive load and improved motivation and knowledge acquisition.

papers.title: Increased encoding of aversive stimuli by lateral habenula neurons during Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol withdrawal.
papers.summary: In rats undergoing Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol withdrawal, calcium photometry and electrophysiology showed increased lateral habenula (LHb) calcium signals, freezing behavior, and excitatory-inhibitory ratios during fear conditioning. Impaired local GABA release and disinhibition of LHb output neurons, including at basal forebrain-LHb inputs, suggest LHb involvement in cannabis withdrawal-associated negative affect.

papers.title: Boder's dyslexia subtypes as a severity continuum with a definitional route axis - A behavioural companion to harmonised qEEG cross-spectra.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology
papers.summary: Analyzed Boder's dyslexia subtypes in 520 children using reading/spelling indices and qEEG cross-spectral connectivity, finding Gaussian-mixture clustering did not align with clinical labels (ARI≈0) and severity was unimodal (dip p=0.36). Subtypes behaved as overlapping regions of continuous distributions; qEEG connectivity separated DD from DYD at AUC 0.85, whereas behavioral classifiers showed weak or non-significant separation once definitional variables were accounted for.

papers.title: SPORADIC CREUTZFELDT-JAKOB DISEASE: CLINICAL FEATURES, DIAGNOSIS AND THERAPEUTIC HORIZONS.
papers.summary: Reviewed literature from October 2015 to October 2025 on sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, synthesizing clinical features, MRI, EEG, CSF biomarkers (RT-QuIC, 14-3-3, total tau), prognosis, differential diagnosis, and management. Diagnosis relies on multimodal integration; no disease-modifying therapy has shown definitive benefit, and management remains supportive.

papers.title: PIP2 binding at allosteric site blocks activation in human rod CNG channels.
papers.summary: Defined the mechanism of PIP2 inhibition of human rod CNG channel CNGA1 using flux assays, single-channel electrophysiology of liposome-reconstituted channels, and cryo-EM structures in lipid nanodiscs. PIP2 binds at the interface between voltage-sensing, pore, and C-linker domains, stabilizing closed states and sterically preventing opening at physiologically relevant ROS membrane concentrations.

papers.title: Isolated Aphasia as an Epileptic Manifestation of Neurosarcoidosis: A Case Report.
papers.summary: Case report of a 23-year-old man presenting with isolated aphasia lasting ~6 hours, recurrent brief episodes, and MRI/EEG/CSF findings consistent with probable neurosarcoidosis with lymphocytic meningoencephalitis and obstructive hydrocephalus. Aphasia resolved with levetiracetam and clobazam, highlighting epileptic aphasia as a rare manifestation of neurosarcoidosis.

papers.title: LifeRhythms: The continuous commitment of the European Heart Rhythm Association in the field of arrhythmias and electrophysiology.
papers.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
papers.summary: This piece describes the European Heart Rhythm Association's LifeRhythms initiative, highlighting its continuous commitment to education and research in arrhythmias and electrophysiology. No abstract was provided, so specific findings or results cannot be summarized.

papers.title: ESC 2025 Madrid: Practice-Changing Trials and What They Mean for Cardiology and Electrophysiology.
papers.journal: Research in heart yield and translational medicine
papers.summary: This editorial reviews practice-changing trials presented at ESC 2025 in Madrid and discusses their implications for cardiology and electrophysiology. It provides a conference-focused perspective rather than original data.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
